invariants: The current single-request ordinary HTTP carrier must announce Connection: close before writing headers; it must not advertise a persistent socket that it always closes.
Connection headers are case-insensitive and cannot contain a conflicting keep-alive declaration; finite bodies and compression remain unchanged.
A standard HTTP client can perform GET then consecutive POST requests by reconnecting before each new request, without a stale-socket abort.
Streaming responses remain open until completion/disposal; raw request-level WebSocket upgrades own their sockets and bypass the ordinary response writer.
open_questions: Node-style persistent HTTP/pipelining and its performance are not implemented by this single-request transport; a future persistence change must also redesign the disconnect monitor.
identity: One accepted TCP ordinary HTTP request owns its response and subsequent close; upgraded sockets have their existing separate owner.
ownership: WebServerService closes ordinary sockets after dispatch; HttpResponseWriter must truthfully signal that lifetime. The Connection disconnect monitor owns only that request.
ordering: Drop every case-variant Connection header, write one canonical close declaration, preserve content/compression, finish the response and drain before socket closure.
errors: A client must not infer HTTP/1.1 persistence and reuse a closing socket for a non-idempotent RPC POST. Browser errors remain asserted, not suppressed or retried to mask transport loss.
cancellation: Server/request disposal still terminates streams and ordinary activity; Connection: close does not prematurely finish an active stream, and upgrade handoff is unchanged.
adaptation: Python 3.8 native one-request carrier uses valid explicit close semantics rather than claiming Node's persistent HTTP implementation. This is a migration transport defect correction, not an upstream bug exception.

rc1_review.scope: Current finite executable provider/consumer corpora, original-browser and extracted observations in the single full receipt. Historical alpha evidence remains historical; no inventory-wide parity, arbitrary ABI/history, paid-provider or Win7 certification.
